Averaging the polynomial over u1,u2 gives [2/r²+1/(cr)+(2/r+1/c)V+V²]Vu4. Using exponential factorial moments then gives m4=24a⁴(40c³+36c²r+21cr²+8r³)/(c⁵r⁶), exactly the stated expression. Their ratio minus three gives the reported K. Its derivative numerator is proportional to a strictly increasing cubic with opposite boundary signs; K−57 has numerator proportional to z(15z²+6z−16) with exactly one positive crossing. Gaussian conditional variance 2DT³/3 gives the comparison 57, and a strictly positive acceleration can match any chosen variance on either branch. The endpoint limits and monotonicity yield exactly two preimages in the claimed open interval. This is not full-law nonidentifiability.
